problems.what: MG90S output-stack height is hard-coded to boss 6.0 + spline 3.0 (spline top 9.0 above the case top) and conflicts with the project's reference envelope nova_v8/cad_head.py micro_servo_local (MS_DOME_H 3.0, MS_SPL_H 2.8, height_with_spline 28.5 -> spline top 5.8 above the case top). The horn stack, hub bore, lip ring, cap arm slot and the step-9 check (arm top 9.3-10.0 from the case top) all depend on this 9.0 and have no adjustability; step 1 does not even measure it.
problems.evidence: build.py servo(): boss = xcyl(5.9, XC-6.0, XC), spl = xcyl(2.4, XC-9.0, XC-6.0); checks.json design_numbers boss_x [-15.9,-9.9], spline_x [-18.9,-15.9], horn_arms_x [-19.5,-17.9]. Repo: nova_v8/spec.py MICRO_SERVO height_with_spline=28.5, body h 22.7; cad_head.py MS_DOME_R, MS_DOME_H = 5.9, 3.0; MS_SPL_H = 2.8. With a repo-shaped servo the hub would seat at x -12.9 and the arm top at ~-16.3, i.e. INSIDE the knuckle (end wall x -16.7..-18.0, hub bore only r4.0): the arms (r6, 5 wide) cannot reach the cap slot x -18.0..-20.15 and usko_kryt cannot be fitted; the step-9 window 0.8-1.5 would be missed by ~3 mm with no remedy. Datasheet figures found online disagree (28.5 vs 31-32 overall) and the two allowed heights differ by 3.2 mm, far beyond the +-0.2 boss tolerance.
problems.fix: 1) Add to montaz step 1: measure boss height (case top -> boss top) and spline top height; record both. 2) Make BOSS_H / SPL_H parameters in build.py (defaults = repo 3.0 / 2.8) and derive XC, hub bore, lip, cap slot and rib positions from them, OR make the -X side tolerant: give usko_kryt a cylindrical plug (r6.4) that enters an r6.6 bore through the knuckle end wall (keep the lip/groove labyrinth outside), with the arm slot inside the plug, so arm tops anywhere from 6 to 10 mm above the case top are accepted. 3) Re-run the sweeps and the step-9 window for both envelopes.

problems.what: The 4 x AWG30 PTFE head wires will not pass the D1.6 wire channel in the +X lug (usko_lozisko) as printed; montaz step 13 has no reaming/dry-fit step and the channel has two kinks (x 20.5 -> 20.3) a drill cannot follow.
problems.evidence: lug_channel(r=0.8): D1.6, ~20 mm long (z 16.5 -> 36.5) with a sphere-kinked tilt between z 21.5 and 26.5. Four round wires of OD 0.56 / 0.60 / 0.64 (typical AWG30 PTFE) pack to a circumscribed D of 1.35 / 1.45 / 1.55 (= (1+sqrt2) x OD); the builder modelled an idealised D1.33 bundle. MSLA prints D1.6 holes 0.1-0.2 undersize (the montaz itself states this rule) -> 1.4-1.5 effective: zero or negative clearance over 20 mm. Walls available: tenon faces at |x| 18.3 / 22.3 (channel at 20.3 -> 1.2 each); the cross-screw pilots stop at y -2.0 so they do not interfere (my distance check 1.53 mm).
problems.fix: Open the channel to a slot 1.6 (x) x 3.0 (y) with R0.8 ends over the whole route (tenon walls stay 1.2, pilots stay >= 1.0 away), keep the tilt, add a 0.5 x 45 lead-in at the chamber end; add to step 13: 'skus nasucho zvazok 4 vodicov cez kanal pred bodom 13; ak neprejde, precisti kanal ihlovym pilnikom / vrtakom D1.7 z oboch koncov'. Alternatively specify wire by OD (<= 0.6 mm) in the BOM.

problems.what: No axial (X) preload of the head: it can float 0.25 mm along the hinge axis with only rib/peg friction holding it.
problems.evidence: -X stop = MR85 inner ring on the neck boss (0 gap); +X stop = usko_kryt inner face (x -18.0) on the neck ledge |x| 17.75: my check 4_cap_dist_neck_tilt0 = 0.25, cap x neck overlap 2.3 mm3 at a +0.3 shift; lip tip/groove bottom 0.4, sleeve end/counterbore floor 0.7. Nothing pushes the head to a defined stop, so the 0.5 hinge seam opens/closes by 0.25 and the head can be wiggled sideways.
problems.fix: Bond a 0.25 mm PTFE (or UHMW tape) thrust ring r8.5..10 on the cap inner face so the running gap to the ledge is ~0.03 and the MR85 inner ring stays on its boss, or add a 0.5 mm closed-cell foam ring between the sleeve end (x 16.5) and the counterbore floor (x 15.8) to preload the head toward -X... choose one stop and preload against it; state it in montaz 14.

problems.what: The display is retained only by 0.36-0.72 N of foam-pad preload; the optional M2x5 screws (18e) are almost certainly impossible on the Waveshare 3.5B (corner holes under the cover glass), so the PCB can lift off its seats under a ~1.5 g bump.
problems.evidence: display weight ~0.5 N (builder), preload 0.36 N (10 kPa foam) to 0.72 N; inserts at ASSUMED holes +-39.75/+-24.75 (head_common HOLE_X/Z) usable only 'if the holes are accessible from the front'. Lateral location by ribs 0.25 is fine; lift-off is limited to the pad spring-back (0.1-0.2 mm) so it is a rattle/touch-offset issue, not a failure.
problems.fix: Add positive retention independent of the foam: two printed hooks on the top/bottom locating ribs overlapping the PCB back edge by 0.8 mm (flex-in on assembly), or a thin backing strap screwed into two of the existing seat inserts; then the 4 inserts in the BOM have a purpose.

problems.what: BOM head-size for the cross screws is not the standard: ISO 7380-1 M2 has dk max 3.8 and k max 1.3, not 3.5 / 1.1 as modelled and written.
problems.evidence: axes 4.0 apart -> 0.2 mm between real heads (model: 0.5); head top at y -12.3 instead of -12.1; my check: still 3.1 mm from the display, no interference. A buyer following 'dk 3.5' will find nothing.
problems.fix: Write 'ISO 7380-1 M2x8, dk <= 3.8, k <= 1.3, hex 1.3' in the BOM and model the heads at 3.8 x 1.3; or move the axes 0.3 further apart (18.0 / 22.6) if a margin > 0.2 is wanted.

problems.what: Capacitive touch of the Waveshare Touch-LCD cannot work through the visor as designed.
problems.evidence: sklo is a solid 5.9 mm slab (y -33.0 -> -27.1, flat back) plus the 0.2 mm air gap to the LCD glass; capacitive controllers on this board are tuned for ~1 mm cover glass. Touch is part of the chosen board but not stated as required.
problems.fix: Either state in SPEC/montaz that touch is not used (display only), or pocket the visor back over the active area (73.4 x 49, leave 1.0-1.5 mm) and bring the LCD to <= 0.3 mm total gap (pads outside the pocket), then re-check the pad and tape numbers.

problems.what: Resin-fit / print notes missing from montaz for several interference or glue-gap features.
problems.evidence: (a) cap arm slot 5.0 with 0.1 ribs: no dry-fit before step 14 (if the slot prints 0.1-0.2 narrow the arms will not enter); (b) head-floor peg holes D2.2 with 3 ribs r0.2: no fit check before step 15 and no instruction not to ream; (c) insert holes D3.4 for OD 3.2 inserts (neck step 3, display 18b): printed undersize ~3.25 leaves no glue gap, no reaming step; (d) print orientation of the neck halves and usko parts not stated (pocket, pin seat and foam recesses must be support-free; supports only on the z -16.5 bottom face since the neck sides are visible); (e) step-16 hex socket is 16 mm behind the window, found blind, with 0.25 mm between the D4 shank and the window edge (my check 2_bit_dist_shell 0.247).
problems.fix: Add: dry-fit cap on arms (sand the ARMS, never the ribs, until firm hand push), dry-fit pegs in the head holes (scrape ribs with a D2.0 drill by hand), 'prevrtaj D3.4' before gluing inserts, print orientations per part, and recommend a D3 shank 1.3 hex bit (or long-arm 1.3 L-key) for step 16 / SERVIS 3.

problems.what: Horn arms can rub the -X knuckle end face at the montaz-allowed minimum arm protrusion combined with the servo's axial float
problems.evidence: Knuckle end face is at x -17.5 (r < 6.8, no relief: the 'sweep' relief xcyl(6.6, -17.5..-18.5) lies outside the neck). Nominal arm back face -17.9 -> 0.4 clearance. montaz step 9 allows the arm face 0.8..1.5 past the lip (x -18.4): at 0.8 the arm back face is at -17.6 -> 0.10 (my hub-height variant hub 3.0: clear_neck 0.10, servo.json). The servo+horn are located axially only by the pocket end walls (+-0.15, foam friction only), so a +0.15 drift gives -0.05 interference and the rotating arm drags on the static knuckle.
problems.fix: In montaz step 9 narrow the allowed protrusion to 1.0..1.5 (arm top 9.5..10.0 below the case top; arm back face <= -17.8), or cut a 0.3 mm relief into the -X knuckle end face for r 2.5..6.6 (end wall stays 1.0 at r<4 is not acceptable there, so prefer the montaz change) and state the servo axial float in the check.

problems.what: The top rabbet-floor ridge was not cleaned (round 5 removed only the bottom one)
problems.evidence: B-rep probe at x 0: material starts at y -26.9 for z 100.6..101.2 and at y -27.0 for z >= 101.3 (local z ~74.25 step). Ray cast on my own tessellation finds 7 slivers 0.021..0.079 thick at (-2.9..5.6, -27.0..-26.96, 101.23..101.25). Same class as the bottom ridge fixed in R5 (clean-up cut only |x|<=12, local z 2.55..3.0). Hidden under the visor flange, prints as a flake.
problems.fix: Add the mirrored clean-up cut in head_pads_and_cuts(): rbox(-12, 12, -27.05, -26.85, HZ+74.0, HZ+74.45) (verify the exact step height with a section at x 0 / 6 / 11.9 as done for the bottom).

problems.what: +X hinge seam (0.5 gap) shows the black lug sleeve from the front and back at eye level
problems.evidence: Face-classified z-buffer (vis2.json): ext0 az0_el0 and az180_el0 show 3.2 mm2 of usko_lozisko interior faces (sleeve r5.54, x 16.5..18.3) through the gap x 17.5..18.0, |y| 1.4..5.5, z 11.5..21.8; 1.8..4.0 mm2 at el -20..+60 and at +-40 tilt. The -X side is closed by the lip ring (not flagged). No internal part (servo, horn, bearing, pin, screws, cables) is visible in any of 320 views.
problems.fix: Optional cosmetic: add a static lip ring on the +X knuckle end (r 6.8..8.0, like LIP) running in a groove of usko_lozisko, or extend the apron box cut from |y|<5.5 to |y|<2.6 so the aprons cover the gap down to the sleeve; otherwise accept as a seam (same width as the -X side).

problems.what: BOM head dimensions for the M2 button-head cross screws are vendor-specific and smaller than some catalogues
problems.evidence: Modelled ISO 7380 M2 dk 3.5 / k 1.1; several vendors list M2 button heads dk 3.8 / k 1.3 (M2 is not in ISO 7380-1). Axes are 4.0 apart, so dk 3.8 still leaves 0.2 between heads, k 1.3 adds 0.2 toward the display (clearance ~10 mm, no issue).
problems.fix: State in the BOM 'dk <= 3.8, k <= 1.3' as the acceptance limit (or specify a source with dk 3.5) so a dk 4.0 head is excluded but common dk 3.8 parts pass.
